label: sweet-search's outside probe is conditional on a sparse gram index: probeOutsideScope returns null unless queryLiterals is available, declines again at or under 800 candidates, and otherwise reads at most 512 candidates (2048 when the scope answered nothing), so its whole design bounds a whole-repo grep and cannot transfer to a lane with no persistent index

lookup-trigger-index.mjs already resolves every document path and score before applying the spec-folder filter, so counting out-of-scope documents and tallying their top-level path segment is one Map increment inside the existing posting loop - no second read, no subprocess, no new index

Measured on this repo: keyed lane scoped to this packet returned 0 docs from 1136 candidate phrases in 0.101s while the same phrase unscoped returned 3 docs in 2 other tracks in 0.107s (+6ms for the hint); ripgrep lane for another phrase was 0.012s scoped vs 0.772s unscoped (64x, a second whole-corpus pass)

No lane emits an out-of-scope signal today: the answer object carries only truncated (a limit fact), so a scoped miss prints results [] beside candidatePhraseCount 1136 and reads as 'this packet knows nothing'; and a repo-wide search finds no caller passing --spec-folder to the keyed lookup, only its own usage comment and archived transcripts, so the scoped keyed lane has no consumer

The two lanes disagree on what a miss means and that decides who needs the line: for 'goal posture rule' the keyed lane returned 0 even unscoped (a declared-phrase miss) while ripgrep returned 31 files unscoped and 0 in scope (a real in-scope absence), so the hint is correct for the ripgrep lane and misleading on the keyed lane's zero

The lesson must be implemented without a persistent index, embeddings, vector/BM25 fusion, an MCP server or a daemon; any variant whose cost model depends on an index (as probeOutsideScope's does) is out of bounds regardless of benefit
